Gian Antonio Grassi was an Italian architect and sculptor who lived from 1723 to 1790. He is known for his work in Baroque and Neoclassical styles. Grassi was born in Bologna, Italy and studied architecture under the guidance of the prominent architect Alfonso Torreggiani.

Grassi is known for his design of several churches and palaces in Italy, including the Church of San Camillo de Lellis in Rome, Palazzo Caprara in Bologna, and the Church of Santa Maria dei Derelitti in Venice. He also worked on various projects in Rome, Milan, and other cities throughout Italy.

In addition to his architectural work, Grassi was also a talented sculptor. He created numerous sculptures that can be found in churches, palaces, and public spaces around Italy.

Overall, Gian Antonio Grassi was a highly respected architect and sculptor during the Baroque and Neoclassical periods in Italy, and his work continues to be admired and studied by art historians and enthusiasts today.
